requirements.original: TemplateBody shall be type compatible with the return type.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a ReplyValue SHALL be type compatible with the return type of the signature.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.4.2 -- TemplateBody shall be type compatible with the return type.

requirements.original: It shall evaluate to a value or template (literal or template instance) conforming to the template(value) restriction.
requirements.canonical: The TemplateBody of a ReplyValue SHALL evaluate to a value or template (literal or template instance) conforming to the template(value) restriction.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.4.2 -- It shall evaluate to a value or template (literal or template instance) conforming to the template(value) restriction.

requirements.original: FieldReference shall not be ParRef
requirements.canonical: The FieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT be a ParRef.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.4.2 -- FieldReference shall not be ParRef

requirements.original: ExtendedFieldReference shall not be TypeDefIdentifier
requirements.canonical: The ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT be a type definition identifier.

ambiguity.issue: TypeDefIdentifier is not a production of the Annex A BNF; it presumably means an Identifier in the ExtendedFieldReference that resolves to a type (the anytype alternative).
readings: No element of the ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL refer to a type definition (e.g. an anytype alternative selection by type name).
The ExtendedFieldReference of a SingleValueSpec SHALL NOT consist solely of a type identifier.

improper_terms.proper: Identifier referring to a type definition

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.4.2 -- ExtendedFieldReference shall not be TypeDefIdentifier

requirements.original: ArrayBounds will resolve to a non negative value of integer type
requirements.canonical: Each array bound (SingleExpression) of an ArrayDef SHALL resolve to a non-negative value of integer type.

ambiguity.issue: 'ArrayBounds' is not a production name; the bounds are the SingleExpressions of ArrayDef (production 424). The comment is placed after ExtendedTypeFieldReference.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.5 -- ArrayBounds will resolve to a non negative value of integer type

requirements.original: The second option is used only for referencing enumerated values,
requirements.canonical: The ReferencedEnumValue alternative of a ReferencedValue SHALL be used only for referencing enumerated values.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- The second option is used only for referencing enumerated values,

requirements.original: in all other cases, the first option is used.
requirements.canonical: A ReferencedValue that does not reference an enumerated value SHALL use the ExtendedIdentifier [ExtendedFieldReference] alternative.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- in all other cases, the first option is used.

requirements.original: ExtendedEnumReference shall be present if and only if Identifier refers to an enumerated value with an attached value list
requirements.canonical: The ExtendedEnumReference of a ReferencedEnumValue SHALL be present if and only if the Identifier refers to an enumerated value with an attached value list.

ambiguity.issue: The ReferencedEnumValue production (441) contains ExtendedTypeFieldReference, not ExtendedEnumReference (442, "(" IntegerValue ")"), so it is unclear which syntax the rule controls.
readings: An enumerated value with an attached value list SHALL be referenced with a parenthesized integer value (ExtendedEnumReference), and other enumerated values SHALL NOT.
The optional ExtendedTypeFieldReference of ReferencedEnumValue SHALL be present if and only if the enumerated value has an attached value list.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- ExtendedEnumReference shall be present if and only if Identifier refers to an enumerated value with an attached value list

requirements.original: A character defined by the relevant CharacterString type. For charstring a character from the character set defined in ITU-T T.50.
requirements.canonical: A Char in a charstring IS a character from the character set defined in ITU-T T.50.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- A character defined by the relevant CharacterString type. For charstring a character from the character set defined in ITU-T T.50.

requirements.original: For universal charstring a character from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.canonical: A Char in a universal charstring IS a character from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- For universal charstring a character from any character set defined in ISO/IEC 10646.

requirements.original: A graphical character from BASIC LATIN or LATIN-1 SUPPLEMENT character sets defined in ISO/IEC 10646 (characters from char (0,0,0,32) to char (0,0,0,126), from char (0,0,0,161) to char (0,0,0,172) and from char (0,0,0,174) to char (0,0,0,255)
requirements.canonical: An ExtendedAlphaNum IS a graphical character from the BASIC LATIN or LATIN-1 SUPPLEMENT character sets of ISO/IEC 10646, i.e. a character from char(0,0,0,32) to char(0,0,0,126), from char(0,0,0,161) to char(0,0,0,172) or from char(0,0,0,174) to char(0,0,0,255).
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- A graphical character from BASIC LATIN or LATIN-1 SUPPLEMENT character sets defined in ISO/IEC 10646 (characters from char (0,0,0,32) to char (0,0,0,126), from char (0,0,0,161) to char (0,0,0,172) and from char (0,0,0,174) to char (0,0,0,255)

requirements.original: Any sequence of newline characters that constitute a newline by using the following C0 control characters: LF(10), VT(11), FF(12), CR(13) (jointly called newline characters, see clause A.1.5.1) from the character set defined in Recommendation ITU-T T.50.
requirements.canonical: An NLChar IS any sequence of the newline characters LF(10), VT(11), FF(12) and CR(13) of ITU-T T.50 that constitutes a newline.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.6 -- Any sequence of newline characters that constitute a newline by using the following C0 control characters: LF(10), VT(11), FF(12), CR(13) (jointly called newline characters, see clause A.1.5.1) from the character set defined in Recommendation ITU-T T.50.

requirements.original: The Identifier refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldOrReference is used is anytype.
requirements.canonical: An Identifier in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference refers to a type definition if the type of the referenced definition in which the ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference is used is anytype.

ambiguity.issue: The rule names 'ExtendedFieldOrReference' (production is ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference) and VarInstance/ReferencedValue, which do not occur in the DefOrFieldRef context of attribute qualifiers.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.1 -- The Identifier refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldOrReference is used is anytype.

requirements.original: IndexRef shall be used when referencing elements of values or arrays.
requirements.canonical: An IndexRef SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference when referencing elements of values or arrays.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.1 -- IndexRef shall be used when referencing elements of values or arrays.

requirements.original: The square brackets with dash shall be used when referencing inner types of a record of, set of or array type.
requirements.canonical: The square brackets with dash "[-]" SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldOrTypeReference when referencing the inner type of a record of, set of or array type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.1 -- The square brackets with dash shall be used when referencing inner types of a record of, set of or array type.

requirements.original: TemplateInstance shall evaluate to a value of a type compatible with the return type for functions returning a value.
requirements.canonical: In a function returning a value, the TemplateInstance of a ReturnStatement SHALL evaluate to a value of a type compatible with the return type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.2 -- TemplateInstance shall evaluate to a value of a type compatible with the return type for functions returning a value.

requirements.original: It shall evaluate to a value, template (literal or template instance), or a matching mechanism compatible with the return type for functions returning a template.
requirements.canonical: In a function returning a template, the TemplateInstance of a ReturnStatement SHALL evaluate to a value, a template (literal or template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the return type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.2 -- It shall evaluate to a value, template (literal or template instance), or a matching mechanism compatible with the return type for functions returning a template.

requirements.original: Within CompoundExpression the ArrayOrMixedExpression can be used for Arrays, record, record of, set and set of types.
requirements.canonical: Within a CompoundExpression, the ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be used' may be a permission or an exhaustive restriction; the lists differ from the parallel rules for BaseTemplateBody and CompoundConstExpression (which omit set). Chose the restrictive reading.
readings: The ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative SHALL only be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types.
The ArrayOrMixedExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of, set and set of types, without excluding other types.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Within CompoundExpression the ArrayOrMixedExpression can be used for Arrays, record, record of, set and set of types.

requirements.original: BooleanExpression shall resolve to a Value of type Boolean
requirements.canonical: A BooleanExpression SHALL resolve to a value of type boolean.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- BooleanExpression shall resolve to a Value of type Boolean

requirements.original: Within CompoundConstExpression the ArrayConstExpression can be used for arrays, record, record of and set of types.
requirements.canonical: Within a CompoundConstExpression, the ArrayConstExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types.

ambiguity.issue: 'can be used' may be a permission or an exhaustive restriction; unlike the CompoundExpression rule, set types are not listed.
readings: The ArrayConstExpression alternative SHALL only be used for array, record, record of and set of types.
The ArrayConstExpression alternative MAY be used for array, record, record of and set of types, without excluding set types.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Within CompoundConstExpression the ArrayConstExpression can be used for arrays, record, record of and set of types.

requirements.original: The TemplateBody on the right hand side of Assignment shall evaluate to an explicit value of a type compatible with the type of the left hand side for value variables
requirements.canonical: When the left hand side of an Assignment is a value variable, the TemplateBody on the right hand side SHALL evaluate to an explicit value of a type compatible with the type of the left hand side.
requirements.condition: the left hand side is a value variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- The TemplateBody on the right hand side of Assignment shall evaluate to an explicit value of a type compatible with the type of the left hand side for value variables

requirements.original: and shall evaluate to an explicit value, template (literal or a template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the type of the left hand side for template variables.
requirements.canonical: When the left hand side of an Assignment is a template variable, the TemplateBody on the right hand side SHALL evaluate to an explicit value, a template (literal or template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the type of the left hand side.
requirements.condition: the left hand side is a template variable
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- and shall evaluate to an explicit value, template (literal or a template instance) or a matching mechanism compatible with the type of the left hand side for template variables.

requirements.original: If more than one XorExpression exists, then the XorExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types
requirements.canonical: If a SingleExpression contains more than one XorExpression, the XorExpressions (operands of `or`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one XorExpression exists, then the XorExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.original: If more than one AndExpression exists, then the AndExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types
requirements.canonical: If a XorExpression contains more than one AndExpression, the AndExpressions (operands of `xor`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one AndExpression exists, then the AndExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.original: If more than one NotExpression exists, then the NotExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types
requirements.canonical: If a AndExpression contains more than one NotExpression, the NotExpressions (operands of `and`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one NotExpression exists, then the NotExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.original: Operands of the not operator shall be of type boolean or derivatives of type Boolean.
requirements.canonical: The operand of the `not` operator in a NotExpression SHALL be of type boolean or a type derived from boolean.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Operands of the not operator shall be of type boolean or derivatives of type Boolean.

requirements.original: If more than one RelExpression exists, then the RelExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.canonical: If an EqualExpression contains more than one RelExpression, the RelExpressions SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one RelExpression exists, then the RelExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types.

requirements.original: If only one RelExpression exists, it shall not derive to a CompoundExpression.
requirements.canonical: If an EqualExpression contains only one RelExpression, that RelExpression SHALL NOT derive to a CompoundExpression.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If only one RelExpression exists, it shall not derive to a CompoundExpression.

requirements.original: If both ShiftExpressions exist, then each ShiftExpression shall evaluate to a specific integer, Enumerated or float Value or derivatives of these types.
requirements.canonical: If a RelExpression contains both ShiftExpressions, each ShiftExpression SHALL evaluate to a specific integer, enumerated or float value or a value of a type derived from these types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If both ShiftExpressions exist, then each ShiftExpression shall evaluate to a specific integer, Enumerated or float Value or derivatives of these types.

requirements.original: Each Result shall resolve to a specific Value.
requirements.canonical: Each BitOrExpression operand of a ShiftExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.

ambiguity.issue: 'Result' is not a production name; the operands of ShiftExpression are BitOrExpressions.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Each Result shall resolve to a specific Value.

requirements.original: If more than one Result exists the right-hand operand shall be of type integer or derivatives
requirements.canonical: If a ShiftExpression contains more than one operand, the right-hand operand SHALL be of type integer or a type derived from integer.

ambiguity.issue: 'Result' is not a production name; the operands of ShiftExpression are BitOrExpressions.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one Result exists the right-hand operand shall be of type integer or derivatives

requirements.original: if the shift op is "<<" or ">>" then the left-hand operand shall resolve to either bitstring, hexstring or octetstring type or derivatives of these types. If the shift op is "
requirements.canonical: If the shift operator is `<<` or `>>`, the left-hand operand SHALL resolve to bitstring, hexstring or octetstring type or a type derived from these types.

ambiguity.issue: 'Result' is used for the BitOrExpression operands. The text is truncated after 'If the shift op is "' - the corresponding rule for the rotate operators `<@` and `@>` is missing (see clause 7.1.5).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- if the shift op is "<<" or ">>" then the left-hand operand shall resolve to either bitstring, hexstring or octetstring type or derivatives of these types. If the shift op is "

requirements.original: If more than one BitXorExpression exists, then the BitXorExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types
requirements.canonical: If a BitOrExpression contains more than one BitXorExpression, the BitXorExpressions (operands of `or4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one BitXorExpression exists, then the BitXorExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.original: If more than one BitAndExpression exists, then the BitAndExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types
requirements.canonical: If a BitXorExpression contains more than one BitAndExpression, the BitAndExpressions (operands of `xor4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one BitAndExpression exists, then the BitAndExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.original: If more than one BitNotExpression exists, then the BitNotExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types
requirements.canonical: If a BitAndExpression contains more than one BitNotExpression, the BitNotExpressions (operands of `and4b`) SHALL evaluate to specific values of compatible types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one BitNotExpression exists, then the BitNotExpressions shall evaluate to specific values of compatible types

requirements.original: If the not4b operator exists, the operand shall be of type bitstring, octetstring or hexstring or derivatives of these types.
requirements.canonical: If the `not4b` operator is present in a BitNotExpression, its operand SHALL be of type bitstring, octetstring or hexstring or a type derived from these types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If the not4b operator exists, the operand shall be of type bitstring, octetstring or hexstring or derivatives of these types.

requirements.original: Each MulExpression shall resolve to a specific Value.
requirements.canonical: Each MulExpression of an AddExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Each MulExpression shall resolve to a specific Value.

requirements.original: If more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp resolves to StringOp then the MulExpressions shall be valid operands for StringOp.
requirements.canonical: If an AddExpression contains more than one MulExpression and the AddOp resolves to StringOp, the MulExpressions SHALL be valid operands for StringOp.
requirements.condition: more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp is StringOp
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp resolves to StringOp then the MulExpressions shall be valid operands for StringOp.

requirements.original: If more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp does not resolve to StringOp then the MulExpression shall both resolve to type integer or float or derivatives of these types.
requirements.canonical: If an AddExpression contains more than one MulExpression and the AddOp does not resolve to StringOp, both MulExpressions SHALL resolve to type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
requirements.condition: more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp is + or -
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one MulExpression exists and the AddOp does not resolve to StringOp then the MulExpression shall both resolve to type integer or float or derivatives of these types.

requirements.original: If only one MulExpression exists, it shall not derive to a CompoundExpression.
requirements.canonical: If an AddExpression contains only one MulExpression, that MulExpression SHALL NOT derive to a CompoundExpression.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If only one MulExpression exists, it shall not derive to a CompoundExpression.

requirements.original: Each UnaryExpression shall resolve to a specific Value.
requirements.canonical: Each UnaryExpression of a MulExpression SHALL resolve to a specific value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Each UnaryExpression shall resolve to a specific Value.

requirements.original: If more than one UnaryExpression exists then the UnaryExpressions shall resolve to type integer or float or derivatives of these types.
requirements.canonical: If a MulExpression contains more than one UnaryExpression, the UnaryExpressions SHALL resolve to type integer or float or a type derived from these types.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- If more than one UnaryExpression exists then the UnaryExpressions shall resolve to type integer or float or derivatives of these types.

requirements.original: Primary shall resolve to a specific Value of type integer or float or derivatives of these types.
requirements.canonical: If a UnaryExpression contains a UnaryOp, its Primary SHALL resolve to a specific value of type integer or float or a type derived from these types.

ambiguity.issue: The rule has no condition, which read literally would restrict every Primary (and thus every expression) to integer or float values; it is only meaningful when the optional UnaryOp is present.
readings: If a UnaryOp is present, the Primary of a UnaryExpression SHALL resolve to a specific integer or float value.
The Primary of a UnaryExpression SHALL always resolve to a specific integer or float value.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Primary shall resolve to a specific Value of type integer or float or derivatives of these types.

requirements.original: The Identifier refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldReference is used is anytype.
requirements.canonical: An Identifier in an ExtendedFieldReference refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldReference is used is anytype.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- The Identifier refers to a type definition if the type of the VarInstance or ReferencedValue in which the ExtendedFieldReference is used is anytype.

requirements.original: IndexRef shall be used when referencing elements of values or arrays.
requirements.canonical: An IndexRef SHALL be used in an ExtendedFieldReference when referencing elements of values or arrays.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- IndexRef shall be used when referencing elements of values or arrays.

requirements.original: DecodedFieldReference shall not appear on the left-hand side of assignments
requirements.canonical: A DecodedFieldReference SHALL NOT appear on the left-hand side of an assignment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- DecodedFieldReference shall not appear on the left-hand side of assignments

requirements.original: DecodedFieldReference shall not appear on the left-hand side of assignments and in type references
requirements.canonical: A DecodedFieldReference SHALL NOT appear in a type reference.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- DecodedFieldReference shall not appear on the left-hand side of assignments and in type references

requirements.original: The Identifier shall resolve into a type
requirements.canonical: The Identifier of a DecodedFieldType SHALL resolve to a type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- The Identifier shall resolve into a type

requirements.original: Operands of the "+" or "-" operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)
requirements.canonical: The operands of the binary `+` and `-` operators (AddOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Operands of the "+" or "-" operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)

requirements.original: Operands of the "*", "/", rem or mod operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)
requirements.canonical: The operands of the `*`, `/`, `rem` and `mod` operators (MultiplyOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).

ambiguity.issue: The rule allows float operands for `rem` and `mod`, while clause 7.1.1 restricts `rem` and `mod` to integer operands.
readings: The operands of `*` and `/` SHALL be integer or float (or derived) and the operands of `rem` and `mod` SHALL be integer (or derived), as in clause 7.1.1.
The operands of `*`, `/`, `rem` and `mod` SHALL all be integer or float (or derived).

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Operands of the "*", "/", rem or mod operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)

requirements.original: Operands of the "+" or "-" operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)
requirements.canonical: The operand of the unary `+` and `-` operators (UnaryOp) SHALL be of type integer or float or a type derived from integer or float (i.e. a subrange).
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Operands of the "+" or "-" operators shall be of type integer or float or derivations of integer or float (i.e. subrange)

requirements.original: Operands of the list operator shall be bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, (universal) character string, record of, set of, or array types, or derivates of these types.
requirements.canonical: The operands of the concatenation operator `&` (StringOp) SHALL be of bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of or array types, or types derived from these types.

ambiguity.issue: The '&' operator is called 'list operator' here, but 'concatenation operator' in clause 7.1.2; '(universal) character string' is used for charstring/universal charstring.

requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- Operands of the list operator shall be bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, (universal) character string, record of, set of, or array types, or derivates of these types.

requirements.original: TemplateInstance-s shall be Identifier-s if the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct (see clause 19.3.2)
requirements.canonical: If the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct, each TemplateInstance of a SelectCase SHALL be an Identifier.
requirements.condition: the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct
requirements.header: // @requirement: A.1.6.8.3 -- TemplateInstance-s shall be Identifier-s if the UnionKeyword is present in the surrounding SelectCaseConstruct (see clause 19.3.2)
